title: Thenar and hypothenar muscles (palmar)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium.
Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
Recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8, T1).
Abducts the thumb, lifting it forward from the palm.
hy: The thenar muscles (Opponens pollicis, Abductor pollicis brevis, Flexor pollicis brevis: OAF) are supplied by the recurrent branch of the median nerve, except that the deep head of flexor pollicis brevis is often supplied by the ulnar nerve. They waste in long-standing carpal tunnel syndrome.

rows: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium.
Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
Recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8, T1). Its deep head is often supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
Oblique head: bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals and the capitate. Transverse head: anterior surface of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal.
Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
hy: Froment sign: with an ulnar nerve lesion the thumb cannot adduct to pinch a sheet of paper, so the patient flexes its tip with flexor pollicis longus instead.

rows: Pisiform and the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris.
Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th digit.
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
Hook of the hamate and the flexor retinaculum.
Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th digit.
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
Flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus in the palm.
Lateral sides of the extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5.
Lateral two: median nerve. Medial two: deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
Flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints.
hy: Loss of the lumbricals causes clawing of the affected fingers: the 4th and 5th in a distal ulnar nerve lesion.

rows: Pisiform and hook of the hamate medially to the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium laterally.
Forms the roof of the carpal tunnel and holds the long flexor tendons in place at the wrist.
hy: The carpal tunnel carries the median nerve and nine tendons (four of flexor digitorum superficialis, four of flexor digitorum profundus, and flexor pollicis longus). Compression of the nerve here is carpal tunnel syndrome. The ulnar nerve and artery pass superficial to the retinaculum.
